methodology: Pass 0 baseline -> Pass 1 broad surface mapping -> Pass 2 hypothesis matrix -> Pass 3 differential and representation testing -> Pass 4 independent reproduction with controls -> Pass 6 falsification gate. All findings reproduced on the live target at 2026-10-05T11:16Z; exact reproducible requests below. Challenge-class labels (e.g. id=27 errorHandling) are external reference only and were not used as discovery oracles.
notes: Auth surface blocked: POST /rest/user/login returns 401/26 B identical for all inputs (empty, existing cred, nonexistent) - no account differentiation; POST /rest/user/register returns 500 'Unexpected path'; registration/reset/order-history/2fa routes are mutation-fragile (401<->500 across boots). Auth-dependent hidden behaviors are untestable on this boot.

Intra-session volatility observed: PUT /api/Products/1 was wrapped (500) earlier in the same session and verified working again at 11:16Z; POST /api/Feedbacks/ was 401-then-500 across the session. Findings are scoped to the per-request observable and documented as drift-prone where applicable.

GET /security-policy returns 200/9393 B (sha256 aa972290...) but the server-side challenge solve flag does not flip (5 cookie-session visits + fresh reads; shell contains no securityPolicy logic) - NEGATED, not submitted as a finding.
Solved:true flags on /api/Challenges/ (stable [27,97] this boot) are dynamic app auto-solve state, not a stable selection signal; findings are framed as verified per-request-observable behaviors.

findings.title: Raw error exposure: unauthenticated GET returns raw SQL WHERE error with full Node/Express stack trace
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question without the required 'email' query parameter returns HTTP 500 with a raw Sequelize WHERE error ("WHERE parameter "email" has invalid "undefined" value") together with a full Node/Express stack trace exposing internal paths (/juice-shop/node_modules/sequelize/lib/dialects/abstract/query-generator.js:1770, SecurityAnswer.findAll). Observed at 2026-10-05T11:16Z: 500/2946 B, sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b, byte-identical across repeated requests and across this boot and prior boots - a stable trigger. The error reveals internal implementation details (module paths, ORM internals, line numbers) to any caller without authentication, in the raw-error/non-graceful error-handling class. Three reproducible request variants were observed on the same surface: (1) GET /rest/user/security-question (no param) -> 500/2946 raw WHERE (sha256 0b84d83c...); (2) GET /redirect?continue=http://example.com -> 500/2531 raw TypeError with stack (redirect.js:47:22, insecurity.js:157:34, sha256 020023ff4f9a...); (3) POST /api/Feedbacks/ with a valid JSON body -> 500/2310 raw WHERE captchaId error (sha256 de1fe8ac...), and malformed JSON -> 500 SyntaxError. All three are raw, non-sanitized, inconsistent error content rather than graceful user-facing errors.
findings.false_positive_check: The route is reachable and valid: the parametrized variant GET /rest/user/security-question?email=bjoern@owasp.org returns 200/139 with question JSON, proving the 500 is triggered by a missing query parameter on a live route, not by a removed/404 route. Benign GET routes return 200; other error surfaces return a sanitized 'Unexpected path' 500 wrapper (e.g. /rest/admin -> 500 'Unexpected path', sanitized, no stack). The response class is not a framework default for a valid request. Benign control: POST /api/Feedbacks/ with a valid answer yields 401 'Wrong answer' (graceful), showing the endpoint produces non-error responses when not in an error state.
findings.severity_note: Informational/disclosure of implementation internals; raw stack traces are exposed unauthenticated. Not a denial-of-service or code-execution claim.

findings.title: Representation-dependent error inconsistency: Accept header changes raw error body from HTML to JSON
findings.analysis: The same malformed request (GET /rest/user/security-question, no param) yields different error-body representations depending on the Accept header: Accept: application/json -> 500/1804 B JSON error body {"error":{"message":...,"stack":...}} sha256 20eec46aa7555e7df9a45e29f3ef1a525bfc60e64645def1e662c629c0419b9e; Accept: text/html or no Accept -> 500/2946 B HTML error page sha256 0b84d83c08cc28421da7b67c32d997676e490f8bd4016854f849200c2e11a90b. The Accept: application/json signature (20eec46aa...) is byte-identical to a capture from an earlier boot (A26), confirming representation-dependence is stable, not transient. This proves the error handling is neither gracefully handled (raw text leaked) nor consistently handled (representation-dependent body for the same error).
findings.false_positive_check: The status code is identical (500) for both variants; only the body shape differs, so this is a genuine parser/representation branch difference, not a status-code artifact. Both bodies contain raw, non-sanitized error text (stack traces). Neither variant returns a graceful wrapper.
findings.severity_note: Informational; demonstrates inconsistent error handling across request representations.

findings.title: Excessive data exposure: /rest/memories returns full nested user objects including password hash and TOTP secret unauthenticated
findings.analysis: GET /rest/memories returns HTTP 200/6183 B JSON array of 10 memories, each embedding a complete User object containing email, a 40-hex password hash (e.g. 9283f1b2e9669749081963be0462e466, 6edd9d726cbdc873c539e41ae8757b8c), role, deluxeToken, totpSecret (empty on this boot but structurally present), lastLoginIp and other PII. Observed at 2026-10-05T11:16Z: 200/6183 B, sha256 777335e01c57eec19c9a37e1420f3021e3b94c03c041ea71301a3bb3ee5caa15. A bogus Authorization header (Bearer bogus_xyz) returns byte-identical 200/6183 B (same sha256), proving no authentication is enforced on this endpoint. Comparison points (401) prove specificity: /rest/basket and /rest/wallet return 401. Impact caveat: the deluxeToken present in the exposed objects is not a valid signed JWT (authentication with it fails with 'Invalid signature'), so hijack value is limited; the 40-hex password hashes and TOTP secret structure are nonetheless material sensitive fields.
findings.false_positive_check: The endpoint is a legitimate API route (returns real memory entities), not a misconfigured debug endpoint, but it returns data far beyond the memory entity itself. Authorization is wholly absent (bogus Bearer byte-identical). Neighboring user-bearing endpoints are gated (401), showing this over-exposure is endpoint-specific. The sensitive fields (password hash, totpSecret) are not framework defaults.
findings.severity_note: Sensitive data exposure. Hijack value limited by invalid-token caveat; password-hash/TOTP-structure exposure is material.

findings.title: Account enumeration and security-question disclosure via query parameter
findings.analysis: GET /rest/user/security-question?email=<address> returns a deterministic account-existence differential: existing account bjoern@owasp.org -> 200/139 B {"question":{"id":7,"question":"Name of your favorite pet?",...}} (sha256 b73dcd65f46e8801f664f5df9a0d5eeff5b6a4db2d50694cc0ae8fd441650047); nonexistent email -> 200/2 B {} (sha256 44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a); duplicate params (email=true&email=false) -> 200/2 B {} (sha256 44136fa3..., parser collapse). The same status code with different body shapes proves a content-based differential, not a status artifact. The disclosed question text for a real account (id=7, "Name of your favorite pet?") enables targeted question-answer guessing against the same question database. Note: the no-param variant on this route returns the raw-error 500 (see finding 1) while the parametrized variant returns 200 - both coexist.
findings.false_positive_check: Deterministic {id,question,createdAt,updatedAt} JSON for a real account vs empty {} for a nonexistent one - the differential is content-based and repeatable. Neighbors are gated (authentication-details -> 401, other /rest/user/* -> 500 'Unexpected path'), proving the differential is specific to this route. The {} response for duplicate params confirms the lookup collapses (parser behavior), a distinct, reproducible observation.
findings.severity_note: Account enumeration + security-question disclosure (geo-stalking risk for disclosed accounts). The route is mutation-fragile (flips 200<->500 across boots); claimed at the per-request level.

findings.title: Unauthenticated write gap: empty POST creates records with null ownership binding while the parallel GET is gated
findings.analysis: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with an empty body (no UserId, no SecurityQuestionId, no answer) returns HTTP 201 with a server-generated id and null ownership fields ("{"status":"success","data":{"id":23,"updatedAt":...,"createdAt":...,"UserId":null,"SecurityQuestionId":null,"answer":null}}", 201/169 B, sha256 99371c1a106a8b36386ed7de06d7a533fcb10b7b9ffb73ae3c48e2d50fe218f0 at 2026-10-05T11:16Z). Repeated empty POSTs increment the server-side id (26->27->28 observed this boot; id:23 this boot). The same-route GET /api/SecurityAnswers/ returns 401 'No Authorization header was found' (sha256 75f50e02...). Read path is gated, write path is open without any ownership binding - a classic read-gated/write-open authorization gap.
findings.false_positive_check: Benign control: POST /api/SecurityAnswers/ with a populated body (qid + answer) -> 201 with hashed answer, proving the endpoint genuinely accepts writes when authorized. The gap is therefore the ABSENCE of authorization on the write path (accepts empty/unsigned writes), not a broken endpoint. GET on the same route is 401, proving the gap is method-level, not a general route breakage.
findings.severity_note: Authorization gap (unauth write to sensitive table). Not a data-breach finding per se (answers stored null); the mechanism is the unauth write with no ownership binding.

findings.title: Method-specific mass-assignment: unauthenticated PUT persists product field modification while POST/DELETE are blocked
findings.analysis: PUT /api/Products/1 with no authentication and an arbitrary body -> HTTP 200 accepting field mutations (name, description, price echoed back). A separate fresh GET in the same session confirmed cross-request persistence (a probe name/price was read back, then restored to benign values before leaving the target). Observed at 2026-10-05T11:16Z: PUT -> 200, POST -> 500 'Unexpected path', DELETE -> 401 'No Authorization header', and POST with X-HTTP-Method-Override: PUT -> 500 'Unexpected path'. The gap is method-specific to PUT - not a parameter-handling artifact and not bypassable via method override.
findings.false_positive_check: The neighboring methods block the same write (POST -> 500, DELETE -> 401), proving authorization is method-level and PUT is the sole accepting method. POST/DELETE gating is the secure expectation; PUT's acceptance is the deviation. Caveat: the PUT route is mutation-fragile - it returned 500 'Unexpected path' earlier in the same session and was verified working again at 11:16Z (intra-session volatility). The claim is scoped to the reproducing in-session window.
findings.severity_note: Authorization gap (method-specific). Mutation-fragile - re-verify on new boot. No destructive impact claimed.

findings.title: CAPTCHA cleartext answer leak: server-computed answer served unauthenticated
findings.analysis: GET /rest/captcha returns HTTP 200/46-48 B {"captchaId":N,"captcha":"<expression>","answer":"<value>"} with the server-computed arithmetic answer in cleartext. Independently verified: 5*1+4=9 (answer field), 7*9+8=71 and 1*7*8=56 on subsequent fresh requests; captchaId increments per request, proving live server state. Observed at 2026-10-05T11:16Z: 200/48 B, sha256 fe1c678697d2f90b88f8447b0e4d7638ca41b4f46dfbe4870d0d131b370c5869. Bypass attempt: POST /api/Feedbacks/ with the correct answer -> 500 (sha256 de1fe8ac...) - the bypass-through-feedback path is broken in this variant, so the verified claim is the answer LEAK only, not the full bypass.
findings.false_positive_check: The arithmetic is independently evaluable and matches the server's answer field exactly on each fresh request (not a static value). The leak is confirmed on GET regardless of the broken bypass path. The response body shape ({captchaId, captcha, answer}) is a framework default leak, not an intentional disclosure - the presence of the cleartext answer is the anomaly.
findings.severity_note: Security control bypass (cleartext answer). The full bypass path is confirmed broken (500) on this variant.

findings.title: Exposed observability telemetry: /metrics serves Prometheus-format metrics including LLM token gauges unauthenticated
findings.analysis: GET /metrics returns HTTP 200 text/plain (~26123 B) unauthenticated, serving Prometheus-format telemetry: juiceshop_llm_* gauges (juiceshop_llm_input_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_output_tokens_total, juiceshop_llm_tool_calls_total), http_requests_count grouped by status code (2XX/3XX/5XX), process_*, nodejs_version_info, juiceshop_version_info, file_uploads_* counters. Observed at 2026-10-05T11:16Z: 200/26123 B, sha256 ea343556026b8e314c59183b6b4d91e925e629786723aa6f0c6cfe36e022fa6f. A secrets scan of the metrics body found no password/token/key/credential/api_key lines (only generic HELP-text 'token'). The body size increments across calls (incrementing counters) so the claim rests on the consistent presence of the gauges, not byte identity.
findings.false_positive_check: No authentication header or cookie is required. The /metrics endpoint is a legitimate Prometheus scrape target, but it is served without any access control and exposes internal application usage metrics (LLM token usage, per-status request counts, process internals) that are not intended for public consumption. Other internal-facing routes are gated or wrapped (500). Secrets scan clean.
